'''Safi R. Bahcall''' (born 1968) is an American physicist, technologist, business executive, and author.

== Early life and academic research ==
Safi Bahcall was raised in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], the son of the physicist [[John Bahcall]] and astrophysicist [[Neta Bahcall]]. From age 13 through 16 he enrolled in physics and mathematics classes at Princeton University. Bahcall received his B.A. from [[Harvard University]] in 1988 in theoretical physics, where he graduated summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa. He received a Ph.D. in physics from [[Stanford University]] in 1995, where he worked with physicist [[Leonard Susskind]] and Nobel laureate [[Robert B. Laughlin]]. He was supported by academic awards including a [[National Science Foundation]]&nbsp;Fellowship, a John Harvard Scholarship, and a National Merit Scholarship. In 1995, he was awarded a Miller Post-Doctoral Research Fellowship at U.C. Berkeley to continue his research in condensed matter theory.

His published work focused on [[superconductivity]], [[random matrix theory]], the [[Quantum Hall effect|quantum hall effect]], and [[particle astrophysics]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Bahcall | first=Safi R. | title=Random Matrix Model for Superconductors in a Magnetic Field | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=77 | issue=26 | date=1996-12-23 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.77.5276 | pages=5276–5279| pmid=10062760 |arxiv=cond-mat/9611136| bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.5276B | s2cid=206326136 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Bahcall | first=Safi R. | title=Boundary Effects and the Order Parameter Symmetry of High-T<sub>c</sub> Superconductors | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=76 | issue=19 | date=1996-05-06 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.76.3634 | pages=3634–3637| pmid=10061017 |arxiv=cond-mat/9603047| bibcode=1996PhRvL..76.3634B | s2cid=45369123 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Bahcall | first=Safi R. | title=Microscopic Description of the Vortex State near the Upper Critical Field | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=75 | issue=7 | date=1995-08-14 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.75.1376 | pages=1376–1379| pmid=10060277 | bibcode=1995PhRvL..75.1376B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bahcall | first1=Safi | last2=Susskind | first2=Leonard | title=Fluid Dynamics, Chern-Simons Theory, and the Quantum Hall Effect | journal=International Journal of Modern Physics B | publisher=World Scientific Pub Co Pte Lt | volume=05 | issue=16–17 | year=1991 | issn=0217-9792 | doi=10.1142/s0217979291001085 | pages=2735–2749| bibcode=1991IJMPB...5.2735B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bahcall | first1=Safi | last2=Gould | first2=Andrew | title=Can cosmic neutrinos be detected by bremsstrahlung from a metal? | journal=Physical Review D | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=43 | issue=3 | date=1991-02-01 | issn=0556-2821 | doi=10.1103/physrevd.43.940 | pages=940–942| pmid=10013456 | bibcode=1991PhRvD..43..940B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bahcall | first1=Safi | last2=Lynn | first2=Bryan W. | last3=Selipsky | first3=Stephen B. | title=New models for neutron stars | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=362 | year=1990 | issn=0004-637X | doi=10.1086/169261 | page=251| bibcode=1990ApJ...362..251B }}</ref>

== Business executive ==
In 1998, Bahcall joined [[McKinsey & Company]], where he advised investment banks and pharmaceutical companies on strategy, technology, and operations. In 2001, he left McKinsey & Company and co-founded, with Lan Bo Chen of the [[Dana–Farber Cancer Institute|Dana-Farber Cancer Institute]], the Boston-based biotech company Synta Pharmaceuticals, which specialized in new drugs to treat cancer and chronic inflammatory diseases. Bahcall led its 2007 IPO on Nasdaq and was Synta's president & CEO for 13 years. In 2016, Synta Pharmaceuticals merged with Madrigal Pharmaceuticals.<ref>{{Cite press release|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20160414005438/en/Synta-Madrigal-Announce-Merger-Agreement-Create-Leading|title=Synta and Madrigal Announce Merger Agreement to Create Leading Cardiovascular-Metabolic Diseases and NASH Company|last=|first=|date=14 April 2016|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

In 2008, Bahcall was named [[Ernst & Young]] New England Biotechnology/Pharmaceutical Entrepreneur of the Year,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ir.madrigalpharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/synta-pharmaceuticals-corps-ceo-safi-bahcall-named-ernst-young|title=Synta Pharmaceuticals Corp.'s CEO Safi Bahcall Named Ernst & Young Entrepreneur Of The Year(R) 2008 Award Winner in New England {{!}} Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc.|website=Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc.|language=en|access-date=2018-08-27}}</ref> In 2010, he and his work were featured in a [[Malcolm Gladwell]] profile in [[The New Yorker]] magazine.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2010/05/17/the-treatment-2|title=The Treatment|magazine=The New Yorker|access-date=2018-08-27|language=en-US}}</ref> He was interviewed by Malcolm Gladwell for the 2012 New Yorker festival, discussing the role of serendipity in science.<ref>{{Citation|last=The New Yorker|title=Dr. Safi Bahcall & Malcolm Gladwell on great scientific discoveries - The New Yorker Live|date=2014-07-22|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4pYW9Q72Y_A|access-date=2018-08-27}}</ref> In 2011, he worked with President Obama's council of science advisors [[United States President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology|(PCAST)]] on the future of US science and technology research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/sites/default/files/microsites/ostp/pcast_future_research_enterprise_20121130.pdf|title=Transformation and Opportunity: The Future of the U.S. Research Enterprise|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

Bahcall has presented at academic institutions and research laboratories including [[Harvard University|Harvard]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], [[Stanford University|Stanford]], [[Princeton University]], [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]], [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Cornell University]], [[Bell Labs]], [[Dana–Farber Cancer Institute|Dana-Farber Cancer Institute]], [[Massachusetts General Hospital]], [[Rockefeller Center|Rockefeller University, the National Institutes of Health]], and the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in Israel, as well as companies and national security organizations including Amazon, Goldman Sachs, Google, Microsoft, Samsung, Spotify, Viacom, the US Air Force, the US Navy, and the CIA.

== Author ==
Bahcall's book ''Loonshots: How to Nurture the Crazy Ideas That Win Wars, Cure Diseases, and Transform Industries'' was released by St. Martin's Press in the Spring of 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://us.macmillan.com/books/9781250185969|title=Loonshots {{!}} Safi Bahcall {{!}} Macmillan|work=US Macmillan|access-date=2018-08-27|language=en-US}}</ref> It was listed on Washington Post's 10 Leadership Books to Watch For in 2019, Inc's 10 Books You Need to Read in 2019, Business Insider's 14 Books Everyone Will Be Reading in 2019, and Adam Grant's New Leadership Books to Look For in 2019. It debuted at #3 on the ''Wall Street Journal'' bestseller list; was an Amazon, ''Bloomberg, Financial Times, Forbes, Inc. Magazine, Management Today, Medium, Strategy + Business, Tech Crunch, Thrive Global, and Washington Post'' best business book of 2019; and was listed for the Thinkers50 and McKinsey-Financial Times Book of the Year awards. ''Loonshots'' was selected by Malcolm Gladwell, Daniel Pink, Susan Cain, and Adam Grant for their Next Big Idea Book Club in the spring of 2019, and by Bill Gates as one of three standout titles in the fall of 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=What Bill Gates is reading now, from 3 standout non-fiction titles to 'every word' written by the late beloved novelist David Foster Wallace|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/books-bill-gates-is-reading-now-david-foster-wallace-2019-9|last=Luce|first=Ivan De|website=Business Insider|access-date=2020-05-18}}</ref> In December 2019, ''Bloomberg'' announced ''Loonshots'' was the most recommended book of the year in its annual survey of CEOs and entrepreneurs.<ref>{{Cite news|title=The Best Books of 2019|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/features/2019-best-books/|last=|first=|date=|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-05-18}}</ref>  A paperback edition of ''Loonshots'' will be published by St. Martin's Griffin on September 1, 2020. ''Loonshots'' has been translated into 18 languages.

In February 2019, Bahcall published a ''Wall Street Journal'' op-ed in response to congressional hearings on the role of federal research in scientific innovation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/if-it-innovates-tax-it-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-suggests-11549583560|title=If It Innovates, Tax It, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Suggests|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>  In February 2020, Bahcall argued in a ''War on the Rocks'' article that the United States should establish a new
